speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your symptoms, can you tell me how long ago these issues started and if they seem to get worse as the day progresses?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the double vision or muscle weakness improve after you rest, and do you have any difficulty swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Do you have any difficulty swallowing, speaking, or breathing, and have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Let me examine your eyes to check for ptosis or any restriction in eye movement. I will also ask you to hold your arms out straight for a minute to see if the weakness worsens with sustained effort.

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I am going to perform a simple bedside test to check for fatigability in your eye muscles. Please look up and hold your gaze there for 30 seconds while I observe for any drooping of your eyelids.

REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibody_Test

speaker: Doctor
text:
The elevated antibody levels confirm the diagnosis of Myasthenia Gravis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
